title: Effect of current guidelines on prevention of pre‐eclampsia with low‐dose aspirin in primary settings: A population‐based case–control study

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec><jats:title>Objective</jats:title><jats:p>To evaluate the effect of low‐dose aspirin, which was administered at or before the 16th week of pregnancy due to maternal characteristics and history of a pre‐existing medical condition, on prevention of pre‐eclampsia, and on the birth of a small‐for‐gestational‐age (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGA</jats:styled-content>) neonate without pre‐eclampsia in nulliparas in primary settings.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Methods</jats:title><jats:p>We performed a case–control study using population‐based data on 47 271 nulliparas with a singleton pregnancy who delivered in Slovenia from 2013 to 2017. The treated group received low‐dose aspirin. For the untreated group, propensity score matching was used to perform a 1:1 matching. In the matched sample, we calculated the odds ratios (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">OR</jats:styled-content>) with a 95% confidence interval (95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content>) with a two‐way test for pre‐eclampsia, as well as <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGA</jats:styled-content> neonates.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>In the treated group (n=584), the odds for an <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGA</jats:styled-content> neonate were significantly increased by 42.7% (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">OR</jats:styled-content> 1.427, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content> 1.001–2.034). However, we found no significant effect on the odds for pre‐eclampsia (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">OR</jats:styled-content> 1.308, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content> 0.847–2.022).</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title><jats:p>In anticipation of more substantial population‐based data studies, in the Slovenian population, preventive treatment with low‐dose aspirin due to maternal characteristics and history of a pre‐existing medical condition is not beneficial for the prevention of pre‐eclampsia and can harm fetal growth.</jats:p></jats:sec>
